Consider the region bounded by the curves $x=6+2y-{y}^{2},$ $x=3{y}^{2},$ and the $x$-axis, as shown above. Calculate the volume $V$ of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis. Do not round the answer.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Now, let $f(y)=6+2y-{y}^{2}$ and $g(y)=3{y}^{2}.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 6+2y-{y}^{2} & =3{y}^{2} \\ 6+2y-4{y}^{2} & =0 \\ 4{y}^{2}-2y-6 & =0 \\ (2y-3)(y+1) & =0 \\ y & =-1,\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution corresponding to our region is $y=\frac{3}{2}.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=\frac{3}{2}.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14258665/assets/9d961b6dbb6b9879b39edc5d4ccbe94f1a0c8146dd8eaf58f8e509d14a23e2fa.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=g(y)=3{y}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=f(y)=6+2y-{y}^{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}y([\text{right}]-[\text{left}])\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3/2}y([6+2y-{y}^{2}]-[3{y}^{2}])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3/2}y(6+2y-4{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3/2}(6y+2{y}^{2}-4{y}^{3})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi (6{\int }_{0}^{3/2}y\,\text{d}y+2{\int }_{0}^{3/2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y-4{\int }_{0}^{3/2}{y}^{3}\text{d}y) \\  & =2\pi ({6\cdot \frac{{y}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{3/2}+{2\cdot \frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{3/2}-{4\cdot \frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{3/2}) \\  & =2\pi (6(\frac{9}{8}-0)+2(\frac{9}{8}-0)-(\frac{81}{16}-0)) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{27}{4}+\frac{9}{4}-\frac{81}{16}) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{63}{16}) \\  & =\frac{63\pi }{8}\end{aligned}
$$
